claim:
For the strongly convex symmetric block quadratic
\[
E_{p,m}(x)=\frac m2\sum_{i=1}^{p}x_i^2+\frac12\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}x_i\right)^2,
\qquad m>0,
\]
apply one exact cyclic alternating-minimization sweep to the globally extrapolated point \(x^k+\alpha(x^k-x^{k-1})\), with fixed \(0\le\alpha\le1\). For two blocks the resulting linear iteration is asymptotically stable for every \(m>0\) and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). For three blocks, put \(c=(1+m)^{-1}\in(0,1)\) and
\[
P_c(\alpha)=1+c+c^2+\alpha c^3(c^2-2c-2)+3\alpha^2c^3(c^2-c-1)+3\alpha^3c^5.
\]
The three-block iteration is asymptotically stable exactly when \(P_c(\alpha)>0\). Let \(c_*\) be the unique root in \((0,1)\) of
\[
7c^4+2c^3-3c^2-2c-1=0,
\]
so \(c_*=0.848972455633114\ldots\) and \(m_*=c_*^{-1}-1=0.177894516323569\ldots\). If \(c<c_*\), every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) is stable; if \(c=c_*\), stability holds exactly for \(\alpha<1\); and if \(c>c_*\), there is a unique \(\alpha_{\rm crit}(c)\in(0,1)\), the unique zero of \(P_c\), and stability holds exactly for \(\alpha<\alpha_{\rm crit}(c)\). In particular, unit extrapolation is stable for every two-block member but is unstable for the three-block family exactly when \(0<m<m_*\), making three blocks minimal for this momentum-instability mechanism.
integrity: The all-parameter result is analytic. A standard-library checker verifies the sweep algebra, Schur--Cohn factorization, threshold isolation, and representative modal root radii; finite checks are corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns exact cyclic block minimization of one symmetric all-to-all quadratic family with one global fixed momentum parameter. It does not cover randomized, restarted, per-block, or auxiliary-sequence accelerated coordinate methods. General extrapolated Gauss--Seidel literature remains a residual terminology-based originality risk.
title: Three blocks create a sharp momentum-stability barrier for cyclic alternating minimization
